title: NJ’s former Lt Gov is using AI to say he’s innocent of sexual harassment
slides: Can AI clear Sheila Oliver's name?
She's using it to fight harassment claims
But AI isn't neutral—it echoes its training
Your reputation could hinge on machine judgment
Ask: who audits the AI that judges you?
thread_text:
1. AI on Trial

A New Jersey official wants AI to clear her name against harassment claims. The machine that judges her is the same one trained on our worst biases.

2. The Tool She Uses

She's using AI to analyze the accusations. But the model can't know her context—only patterns from data it was fed.

3. Bias Doesn't Disappear

AI isn't neutral. It echoes its training. If the data is sexist, the judgment will be too—just with a math label.

4. Your Turn Next

Reputation, job, freedom—all could hinge on machine judgment. And you won't get to cross-examine the algorithm.

5. Who Audits the AI?

Take a prompt on ChatGPT: ask it to judge a harassment case. If you haven't tested the bias yourself, start there.

instagram.caption:
A former New Jersey lieutenant governor is using AI to argue she's innocent of sexual harassment claims.

She's feeding the accusations into a model to back her defense.

But AI isn't neutral—it echoes whatever patterns it was trained on, including sexist ones. ⚖️

So the same machine judging her reputation is built from data full of our worst biases.

If you publish or create content, your credibility could soon rest on an algorithm you can't question.

Next time you ask ChatGPT to judge a harassment case, remember: who actually audits the AI deciding your fate? 🤖
